content: Retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG, is a technique that grounds a language model's answer in documents fetched at query time. The retriever first searches an index or the web for passages relevant to the question. Those passages are then placed into the model's context so the answer can cite them directly. RAG reduces hallucination because the model is asked to synthesise provided evidence instead of relying only on its training data. Production systems usually add a reranking step that orders candidate passages by relevance before generation.
title: Sample: What is retrieval-augmented generation?

content: Citations let a reader verify an AI-generated claim in seconds instead of trusting the model blindly. A 2025 survey of enterprise buyers found that verifiability ranked among the top requirements for adopting AI research tools. Inline citations also create an audit trail, which regulated industries such as finance and healthcare require before deployment. Systems that attach a source marker to every factual sentence are measurably easier to fact-check than systems that list sources only at the end.
title: Sample: Why citations matter in AI answers

content: NVIDIA's Nemotron family is a line of open-weight language models released for commercial use. The family spans small Nano models for fast everyday calls and larger Super and Ultra models intended for heavier reasoning workloads. Nemotron models are served by several inference providers, including Nebius Token Factory, through an OpenAI-compatible API. Open weights let teams inspect, fine-tune, and self-host the same model they prototype against in the cloud.
title: Sample: Open-weight models and the Nemotron family

content: Agent frameworks typically get fresh web knowledge from a search API rather than scraping pages themselves. Tavily is one such API, designed for AI applications, returning cleaned content snippets ranked by relevance. Search results usually include a title, a URL, a relevance score, and sometimes a publication date. Agents combine search with an extraction step when a snippet is too short to support a claim.
title: Sample: Web search APIs for agents

content: Unverified AI output creates rework: a human must re-derive every number before it can be used in a report. Analysts report spending a significant share of their AI-assisted research time on verification alone. Tools that surface evidence next to each claim shift verification from re-derivation to spot-checking. That shift is why citation-first interfaces are becoming the default for research copilots.
title: Sample: The cost of unverified AI output
